name: mixteco de Magdalena Peñasco
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.

catalog_quote: Las palabras del mixteco tienen un núcleo de dos sílabas con el acento prosódico en la primera. Este grupo bisílabo es de mucha importancia en la fonología de la lengua, y se presentan los tonos de este grupo antes de considerar las palabras más largas o más cortas. ... El tono bajo, cuando recibe el acento prosódico, que cae en la primera sílaba del grupo bisílabo, se actualiza como un desliz del tono medio al tono bajo. ... la palabra compuesta de tres sílabas nd¢k¢tª ‘lavar’ tiene el acento prosódico en la sílaba k¢ ... Las palabras nativas de tres sílabas son todas formas compuestas. La mayoría se compone de un prefijo más una raíz de dos sílabas. ... Los préstamos del español han entrado al mixteco con varios patrones tonales, según el acento prosódico de la palabra en español. En su forma mixteca, la gran mayoría de estas palabras tiene el acento prosódico en la penúltima sílaba, …

new_statements.quote: Las palabras del mixteco tienen un núcleo de dos sílabas con el acento prosódico en la primera. [p.1] ... El tono bajo, cuando recibe el acento prosódico, que cae en la primera sílaba del grupo bisílabo, se actualiza como un desliz del tono medio al tono bajo. [p.2] ... la palabra compuesta de tres sílabas nd¢k¢tª ‘lavar’ tiene el acento prosódico en la sílaba k¢ [p.6] ... En su forma mixteca, la gran mayoría de estas palabras tiene el acento prosódico en la penúltima sílaba, de acuerdo con los patrones para palabras nativas. [p.33] ... Hay un grupo de palabras funcionales (partículas) que no reciben un acento prosódico, y tienen una sola vocal. [p.35]
new_statements.translation: Mixtec words have a nucleus of two syllables with the prosodic stress on the first. [p.1] ... Low tone, when it receives the prosodic stress, which falls on the first syllable of the bisyllabic group, is realized as a glide from mid tone to low tone. [p.2] ... the three-syllable compound word nd¢k¢tª 'to wash' has the prosodic stress on the syllable k¢ [p.6] ... In their Mixtec form, the great majority of these words [Spanish loans] have the prosodic stress on the penultimate syllable, in accordance with the patterns for native words. [p.33] ... There is a group of function words (particles) that do not receive a prosodic stress and have a single vowel. [p.35]

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: the PDF's metadata: 47 pp., CreationDate Apr 2004; front matter '[mayo 2004] (c) 2004 Instituto Lingüístico de Verano'). Re-extracted every page with extracted text and searched for acento/acentuada/átona. All five quoted sentences are verbatim at the stated pages: p.1 sec.1.1 'Las palabras del mixteco tienen un núcleo de dos sílabas con el acento prosódico en la primera.'; p.2 sec.1.2 'El tono bajo, cuando recibe el acento prosódico, que cae en la primera sílaba del grupo bisílabo, se actualiza como un desliz del tono medio al tono bajo.'; p.6 sec.2.1 'la palabra compuesta de tres sílabas nd¢k¢tª ‘lavar’ tiene el acento prosódico en la sílaba k¢'; p.33 sec.3.2 'En su forma mixteca, la gran…
new_statements.relation_note: This is the very source the catalog record (penultimate stress, penult) was built from; all five quoted sentences were re-read in the text we hold layer at the stated pages and match the catalog quote verbatim. The catalog's date '2005' (from the Glottolog listing) differs from the PDF's own '[mayo 2004]'; the the full catalog already carries the corrected 2004 date and 47 pp. The only caveat is that the '0010' cell for four-syllable words rests on the loan 'presidente' and the author's penult equation, not on an explicit statement about native four-syllable compounds.
new_statements.rule_in_words: There is no separate stress section; stress (acento prosódico) is stated inside the tone description. Every native word is built on a bisyllabic root couplet stressed on its first syllable; native trisyllables are prefix + couplet, so stress sits on the root-initial syllable (nd¢-k¢-tª stressed on k¢), which is the penult of the word. Spanish loans of 2-4 syllables (libro, Castilla, barato, presidente) overwhelmingly take penultimate stress, which the author explicitly equates with the native pattern. Monosyllabic particles (proclitics, enclitics) carry no stress and are written as separate words. Native 4- and 5-syllable compounds (sec. 3.1 pp.32-33) are listed with tone patterns only; their stress position is not stated, so word lengths above three rest on the loan example plus the author's penult equation. Stress coexists with three-level lexical tone and conditions its realization (stressed low = mid-to-low glide; unstressed mid syllables are the targets of low-tone spreading). No weight conditioning is mentioned.
new_statements.exceptions: fn.6 p.7 (hedged): 'Es muy probable que el tono alto en la última sílaba haya atraído el acento prosódico a ésta, y la sílaba penúltima se percibe como otra sílaba átona que se deja cambiar al tono bajo' (final high tone in m.a(b) words may attract stress to the final syllable). Sec. 2.1 p.7: 'A veces un verbo copulativo se pronuncia sin acento prosódico y las dos sílabas se cambian al tono bajo.' fn.14 p.33: 'Las personas menores de edad y más bilingües en español pronuncian estas palabras [préstamos esdrújulos] con el acento prosódico en la sílaba antepenúltima, como en español'. Sec. 3.3 p.35: monosyllabic particles are unstressed.
new_statements.identity_note: Work 1 describes the Mixtec of the municipio of Magdalena Peñasco, distrito de Tlaxiaco, Oaxaca (fn.1 p.1); fn.13 (p.29) notes that the neighbouring San Cristóbal Amoltepec variety, and some speakers in northern Magdalena, lack one prefix-root tone restriction. The site bibliography notes that the same glottocode also groups Santo Domingo Huendio (Becerra Roldán 2015, not yet obtained), for which no stress statement has been checked. Work 0's author Barbara E. Hollenbach is the same person as Elena Erickson de Hollenbach.

Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology / University of California Santa Barbara, 15 August 2022. tone_statements.quote: Los tres niveles de tono son alto, medio y bajo; se abrevian a, m, b, y se simbolizan en la forma á, ¢, ¤. Cada vocal se pronuncia con uno de estos tonos. No hay deslices de un tono a otro en una sola vocal en las formas básicas de las palabras. … Cuando una de estas palabras se pronuncia en forma aislada, hay ocho combinaciones; de las nueve posibles combinaciones, todas pueden presentarse excepto bajo bajo. … A estos tonos se les llaman tonos flotantes. En el mixteco de Magdalena Peñasco, son tres diferentes.
tone_statements.translation: The three tone levels are high, mid and low; abbreviated a, m, b and written á, ¢, ¤. Each vowel is pronounced with one of these tones. There are no glides from one tone to another on a single vowel in the basic forms of words. … When one of these words is pronounced in isolation there are eight combinations; of the nine possible combinations all occur except low low. … These tones are called floating tones. In Magdalena Peñasco Mixtec there are three different ones.
tone_statements.locator: p. 1, section 1.1 Tonos contrastantes, and p. 2, section 1.3 Tonos flotantes
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (high, mid, low), one per vowel, no contours in basic forms; no low-low couplet; three floating tones drive progressive sandhi; H, M lowered after L; stress on 1st couplet syllable.

tone_statements.citation: Hollenbach, Barbara E. (2007). Tone languages and language (un)awareness. SIL Forum for Language Fieldwork 2007-004. 3 pp.
tone_statements.quote: El mixteco es una lengua tonal, pero sus hablantes manejan los tonos de manera inconsciente. … A la palabra principal, entre corchetes, le sigue una representación de los tonos que tiene la forma básica de la palabra, usando las letras a (tono alto), m (tono medio) y b (tono bajo). … Las letras (a), (b) y (ba) entre paréntesis, al final de la representación tonal, indican un tono que se mueve a la palabra de la derecha (estos tonos se llaman tonos flotantes)
tone_statements.translation: Mixtec is a tonal language, but its speakers handle the tones unconsciously. … The headword is followed, in square brackets, by a representation of the tones of the basic form of the word, using the letters a (high tone), m (mid tone) and b (low tone). … The letters (a), (b) and (ba) in parentheses at the end of the tonal representation indicate a tone that moves to the word on the right (these tones are called floating tones)
tone_statements.locator: p. xxi 'El alfabeto' and p. xxiii 'Cómo usar este diccionario: Cómo usar la parte mixteco—español'; tone glide and variable high on p. xxiv; verb tone in 'Conjugaciones básicas de los verbos: Introducción' pp. 869-870
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (high, mid, low) written per syllable on every entry; floating tones dock on the next word; glides are tone sequences on one syllable; present/subjunctive marked by a floating high.

tone_statements.quote: There are three levels of tone, high, mid, and low. When low occurs on a syllable with either primary or secondary stress, it is realized as a mid‑low glide. … In addition to the three levels, there are three floating tones, high, low‑high, and low, each of which affects the following word in its own way. … Tone carries a fairly heavy functional load. Not only does it differentiate many lexical sets, but a floating high tone preceding a verb also marks the grammatical categories present tense and subjunctive mood.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 10-11, sec. 3.2 Tone; mora statement p. 9 'Note on long and interrupted vowels'
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (high, mid, low), one per vowel mora, plus floating high, low-high and low tones altering the next word; low under stress is a mid-low glide; tone marks tense; root-initial stress.

tone_statements.citation: Hollenbach, Barbara E. (2003). The historical source of an irregular Mixtec tone-sandhi pattern. In Language and life: Essays in memory of Kenneth L. Pike. SIL International & University of Texas at Arlington. pp. 533–550.
tone_statements.quote: El mixteco es una lengua tonal, es decir, hay palabras que tienen las mismas vocales y consonantes, pero que tienen diferentes tonos, por lo tanto son diferentes palabras. La gente de Magdalena habla una variante de la lengua que tiene tres niveles de tono: alto (á), medio (ā) y bajo (a). ... Para expresar el tiempo presente, el tono medio de la primera sílaba cambia a tono alto ... Además, el tono de algunas palabras produce cambios en la palabra siguiente.
tone_statements.translation: Mixtec is a tonal language, that is, there are words that have the same vowels and consonants but different tones, and are therefore different words. The people of Magdalena speak a variety of the language that has three tone levels: high (á), mid (ā) and low (a). ... To express the present tense, the mid tone of the first syllable changes to high tone ... In addition, the tone of some words produces changes in the following word.
tone_statements.locator: live pagehttps://mexico.sil.org/es/lengua_cultura/mixteca/mixtecomagdalena,section 'Rasgos lingüísticos' > 'Una lengua tonal' (page footer (c) 2026 SIL Global)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: 3 levels H M L; grammatical tone (present = M>H on syllable 1); rightward H-docking sandhi.

tone_statements.citation: Erickson de Hollenbach, Elena. n.d. [site (c) 2023; Internet Archive copy 2024]. Mixteco de Magdalena Peñasco (código xtm de la ISO). SIL México, Lengua y Cultura: Familia mixteca (language profile web page, with audio examples).
tone_statements.quote: The data for this variety comes from an extensive, recently published dictionary by Hollenbach (2017) using a latin-based system. Tones are not marked on the entry but given in square brackets after the entry, represented with letters; ... There are three level tones (low, mid, high) and one contour (rising). The level tones all combine with each other, except there is no low-low combination. The contour tone only appears on the second mora and in our data set only combines with the high tone. This results in 9 contrastive tone melodies. The glottal stop has no influence on tone reflexes. Generally, *H has mid tone reflex, and *L has a low tone reflex.
tone_statements.locator: p. 6, section 'Group 3' > 'Magdalena Peñasco Mixtec'; Table 9 'Constrastive tone melodies in Peñasco Mixtec' floats at the top of the same page; Huendío paragraph + Table 10 follow
tone_statements.summary: 3 levels (1=L, 3=M, 5=H) + rising 15 on mora 2; 9 couplet melodies; no LL; *H > M, *L > L; TBU mora.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim in the held 2004 SIL tone paper at all stated locators. The classification (stress on the first syllable of the bisyllabic root = penult of the orthographic word; loans mostly penult) rests on a first-hand phonology article by the language's describer, and the best available source, her 2013 475-pp reference grammar, is already held by the project and independently states the same rule in sec. 2.5 pp.22-23 (stress always on root-initial syllable; penult in words ending in a plain vowel; first mora of a final long/glottalized vowel; clitics unstressed and written separately; 'el acento es muy regular'). Nothing in either source suggests a different coding; the only nuances (CVV-final roots stressed on the first part of the vowel; weak stress sometimes heard on a H-toned final syllable; bilingual speakers' Spanish-pattern loans) are already compatible with the record's the primary-stress rule/ex

tone.quote: The Mixtec languages from southern Mexico provide an ideal starting point for studies in this area, as they are all tonal and tone can be reconstructed to the proto-language. … This means that the tones represented in the database are contrastive, i.e. they are tonemes rather than phonetic tones. Tone correspondences were established based on the comparative method … I included all Mixtec varieties for which tonal contrasts were marked systematically and in a reliable way.

tone.quote: These languages are all tonal and tone carries a high functional load both in lexicon and grammar. … Before discussing the methodology of establishing tone change variables, I cover the basics of Mixtec tone systems and summarize two earlier studies of Mixtec tone reconstruction. The tone-bearing unit (TBU) in Mixtec is the mora, which means that each ‘couplet’ has two tones. These two tones can be level or contour tones, depending on the variety.

tone.quote: El mixteco es una lengua tonal, es decir, hay palabras que tienen las mismas vocales y consonantes, pero que tienen diferentes tonos, por lo tanto son diferentes palabras. La gente de Magdalena habla una variante de la lengua que tiene tres niveles de tono: alto (á), medio (ā) y bajo (a). ... Para expresar el tiempo presente, el tono medio de la primera sílaba cambia a tono alto ... Además, el tono de algunas palabras produce cambios en la palabra siguiente.
tone.locator: live pagehttps://mexico.sil.org/es/lengua_cultura/mixteca/mixtecomagdalena,section 'Rasgos lingüísticos' > 'Una lengua tonal' (page footer (c) 2026 SIL Global)
tone.translation: Mixtec is a tonal language, that is, there are words that have the same vowels and consonants but different tones, and are therefore different words. The people of Magdalena speak a variety of the language that has three tone levels: high (á), mid (ā) and low (a). ... To express the present tense, the mid tone of the first syllable changes to high tone ... In addition, the tone of some words produces changes in the following word.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: 3 levels H M L; grammatical tone (present = M>H on syllable 1); rightward H-docking sandhi.
tone.says: Three tone levels high (á), mid (ā), low (a); grammatical tone - present tense formed by raising the first-syllable mid tone to high; tone sandhi - a word-final high tone of nda'á detaches and docks on the first vowel of the following word displacing its low tone; tone is not written in the practical alphabet.
